## LitAnatomy v0.1.0

The first release: a place to organise, dissect and cite the papers of a literature review.

### Adding papers
- **By DOI:** paste one or many DOIs, in any form ("DOI: 10.1109/…", "https://doi.org/…", "Digital Object Identifier 10.…"). The details come from doi.org, with Crossref as a fallback.
- **From files:** BibTeX, BibLaTeX, RIS (EndNote, Mendeley, Zotero, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore), RefWorks and CSL-JSON. A preview shows each reference, its new key and any that are already in your library, before anything is added.
- **Duplicates:** found by DOI or by title and year. Use the existing paper, fill in its missing details, or import a new copy.

### Dissecting papers
- **Anatomy fields:** Problem & Motivation, Contribution, Methodology, Key Findings, Key Metrics, Limitations, Research Gaps & Future Work, Critical Assessment (with a 1–5 rating), Key Quotes (with page numbers), Relevance to This Project and Further Notes. Rename, reorder or hide them in Settings.
- **Per-collection fields:** a collection can have its own extra fields, such as "Frequency range".
- **Relevance per project:** a paper can matter for different reasons in different collections, so its relevance note is kept per collection.
- **Autosave:** notes are saved as you type, and written as Markdown.

### Organising
- **Collections and sub-collections** for each piece of work: a first-year assessment, a paper, a thesis chapter, your viva. Drag papers onto them in the sidebar.
- **Reading status** (to read, reading, summarised), tags, links between papers ("builds on", "contradicts", …) and full-text search across titles, authors and notes.
- **Synthesis matrix:** compare papers side by side and export the table to CSV, Markdown or LaTeX.

### Citing
- **Readable keys** such as `zhang2025Wideband`, from a pattern you can change. Numeric keys from IEEE Xplore and similar are replaced on import.
- **Stable keys:** once exported, a key is pinned and never changes on its own.
- **Export .bib** for a collection or a selection, as BibTeX or BibLaTeX.
- **Auto-export** (Settings): keep each collection's .bib file up to date, e.g. in your thesis folder.

### Also
- **PDFs:** link each paper to its PDF and open it in your usual viewer. With a PDF folder set, links still work on another computer.
- **Themes:** light, dark or follow the system, in six colour themes, with adjustable text size.
- **One file:** your whole library is a single file you can back up or keep in a synced folder.
